$comment: Who keeps each kind of camp, and what they are doing at each stretch of the day. Read by
src/content/campLife.ts; the hours are in src/content/tiers.ts (CAMP_DAY), never here.
Three people a camp: the one who leads, a follower who is also the camp's runner to the road, and
a follower who keeps the fire at night. Bodies are the strangers' painted sheets, dyed per person
by looks.ts, so no art is needed. Cultures are canon's own ids; names come from canon's peoples.
Nobody here is a threat to anybody, on the owner's ruling: no weapon is held up in any line, the
dacoits' toll is an arrangement with the salt carriers, and nobody follows the player.
`doing` finishes the sentence '{name} ...'. A string, or one per slot.
`says` is one line each, said when you talk to them. `trades` is what the runner carries to or
from the road, and `eats` is the meal, for the line when you sit and eat with them.
`road` is what the talk row says about somebody on the road who is busy with a camp: a visitor sitting at
its fire, or a traveller stopped at the turn-off trading with its runner. `{who}` is how the row names
them; `{trades}` is the camp kind's own `trades`.

leader.title: head drover
leader.about: head drover, who keeps the fold

runner.title: gate-mender
runner.about: gate-mender, a coil of withies on one shoulder

watch.title: milker
watch.about: milker, with a pail that is never quite empty

doing.pitch: is setting the hurdles of the fold upright, one by one
doing.relight: is blowing last night's fire back into flame

chore.leader: is walking the line of the fold, counting under their breath
chore.runner: is lashing a gap in the hurdles shut
chore.watch: is milking at the fold, cheek against a warm flank

doing.shade: is sitting out the heat in the shade of the tent
doing.meal: is eating by the fire, a bowl held in both hands
doing.evening: is counting the goats in through the gate as the light goes
doing.watch: is keeping the fire while the others sleep
doing.strike: is rolling up the felt of the tent
doing.road: is walking out toward the road with a bundle of hair
doing.trade: is trading goat hair for flour at the road
doing.home: is walking back from the road with a sack of flour

says.leader: Grass is short this year, so we keep moving. Three days here, and then the next hollow.
says.runner: Every gate we make, the goats find the one weak withy. Every one.
says.watch: Sit down, sit down. There is always milk.

drovers.eats: Milk still warm from the fold and millet cakes off the hot stones. You eat until you are told to stop, and you are not told.

runner.title: lamp-keeper
runner.about: lamp-keeper, with oil on the fingers

doing.pitch: is stretching the cloth of the shelter between two poles
doing.relight: is coaxing the fire alight, singing to it very quietly

chore.leader: is tying new strips of cloth to the pole, one for each of them
chore.runner: is trimming the wick of the lamp on the cairn
chore.watch: is picking stones out of the rice

doing.shade: is resting in the shade of the cloth, eyes closed but not asleep
doing.meal: is eating by the fire, slowly, and not talking
doing.evening: is singing with the others, the lamp lit on the cairn
doing.watch: is keeping the fire and the lamp while the others sleep
doing.strike: is folding the cloth of the shelter small
doing.road: is walking out toward the road with an empty oil jar
doing.trade: is buying lamp oil at the road
doing.home: is walking back from the road with the oil jar full

says.leader: We will not tell you where we are going. It is not a secret. It is only that it does not sound like much, said out loud.
says.runner: The lamp must not go out between here and there. That is the whole of my job, and it is enough.
says.watch: Rice and ghee, every day. Nobody complains, because then they would have to cook.

pilgrims.eats: Rice and ghee from a shared pot, and somebody hums while you eat. It is the best rice you have had in a month.

leader.title: one with the map
leader.about: the one with the map, which is not finished

runner.title: rope-hand
runner.about: rope-hand, with more rope than sense

watch.title: cook
watch.about: cook, who also argues about the map

doing.pitch: is propping up the lean-to, and then propping it up again
doing.relight: is poking the fire and blaming the wood

chore.leader: is adding a line to the map, and rubbing it out
chore.runner: is coiling rope that does not want to be coiled
chore.watch: is stretching a hide on the rack

doing.shade: is lying in the shade of the lean-to, map over their face
doing.meal: is eating by the fire and pointing at the map with a flatbread
doing.evening: is arguing over the map by firelight, cheerfully
doing.watch: is keeping the fire, with the map, while the others sleep
doing.strike: is pulling down the lean-to, which comes down more easily than it went up
doing.road: is walking out toward the road to buy flour
doing.trade: is buying flour at the road and asking about the ground ahead
doing.home: is walking back from the road with flour and news

says.leader: Three of us, three opinions about this map. You look like somebody with a fourth.
says.runner: Never trust a ford you have only heard about. Never trust a rope you did not coil yourself.
says.watch: It is burnt on one side. That is the side with the flavour.

adventurers.trades: flour, and news of the ground ahead
adventurers.eats: Flatbread, burnt on one side as promised, and something stewed that nobody will name. It is very good.

leader.title: headman
leader.about: headman, who only looks and waits

watch.title: tally-keeper
watch.about: tally-keeper, a knotted cord in hand

doing.pitch: is hanging the hides of the shelter, quickly, out of long practice
doing.relight: is building the fire up from last night's coals

chore.leader: is sitting where the whole valley can be seen, watching it
chore.runner: is stacking the salt sacks, and restacking them
chore.watch: is knotting the day's toll into a cord, and losing count

doing.shade: is sitting out the heat under the hides
doing.meal: is eating by the fire, and passing the pot along without being asked
doing.evening: is counting the day's toll with the others, badly, and laughing about it
doing.watch: is keeping the fire while the others sleep, and nods to you
doing.strike: is pulling the hides down and rolling them tight
doing.road: is walking out toward the road to meet the salt carriers
doing.trade: is taking the salt carriers' toll at the road, which is an old arrangement
doing.home: is walking back from the road with a sack of salt over one shoulder

says.leader: We hold the ford in the dry months. The salt carriers pay, and the ford stays clear for them. You, we do not charge. You have nothing we want, and that is meant kindly.
says.runner: I wave at everybody. It saves a lot of misunderstanding.
says.watch: Twelve sacks. Or eleven. It is never the same number twice, and nobody minds but me.

dacoits.eats: Salted fish, and more of it than you expected. They are poorer than they would like you to think, and they share it anyway.

road.visit: {Who} has come out to the camp to eat, and for {trades}.
road.trade: {Who} has stopped at the turn-off to trade with the camp's runner: {trades}.
